article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: OGKB Blueberry Headband × Grape Gas
Breeder: Compound Genetics
THC Content: 24-27%
CBD Content: Typically low
Terpene Profile: myrcene , beta-caryophyllene , linalool
Primary Flavors: Sweet grape, blueberry, candy
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September through Octobert
Indoor Yield: Medium
Outdoor Yield: Medium
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

El Chivo is the kind of cannabis cross that makes its reputation before the smoke ever reaches the consumer. Mature flowers can develop deep coloration beneath a nearly continuous coating of trichomes, while the aroma moves rapidly from sweet grape and blueberry into candy, perfume, and kerosene-like fuel. Compound Genetics originally released the cultivar in its Grape Gas collection, pairing OGKB Blueberry Headband with Grape Gas and creating a seed line that became especially famous after one exceptional phenotype—El Chivo #5—was selected and later circulated as Glitter Bomb . That distinction matters because Glitter Bomb is one celebrated cut from El Chivo rather than a separate original pedigree.

Beyond its visual appeal, the line earned attention for unusually dependable garden traits. Compound Genetics describes most phenotypes as having long internodal spacing with distinct individual bud sites, allowing light and air to penetrate more easily than in heavily congested plants. An 8–9-week flowering period, average vegetative pace, strong resin production, and generally cooperative growth make the cultivar accessible without reducing its appeal to experienced phenotype hunters. For growers interested in grape-and-gas marijuana with serious bag appeal, El Chivo has become one of the more influential Compound Genetics releases of its generation.
Genetics and Lineage

The official pedigree is OGKB Blueberry Headband × Grape Gas. The female side combines OGKB influence with Blueberry Headband characteristics, bringing berry sweetness, dense resin, and a deeper Kush-oriented foundation. OGKB , short for OG Kush Breath, is closely associated with the Cookies family and contributes compact flower structure, earthy dessert qualities, and strong potency. Blueberry Headband adds another layer of berry expression while carrying Headband-style fuel and a more expansive hybrid character. Together, those traits provide a complex base rather than a simple blueberry-flavored parent.

Grape Gas supplies the second half of the cross and is responsible for much of El Chivo’s unmistakable grape-fuel identity. The line combines Grape Pie with Jet Fuel Gelato , linking sweet purple-fruit genetics with the pungent gas, creamy Gelato, and resin production associated with modern fuel hybrids. Compound’s breeding work around Grape Gas produced numerous crosses, but El Chivo became one of the standouts because the fruit character remained clear without allowing the fuel component to disappear beneath sweetness.

One phenotype eventually became more famous than the seed line itself. El Chivo #5 was selected for extraordinary trichome coverage, rich purple calyxes, strong stems, impressive flower quality, and a loud grape-and-gas profile. That plant became known as Glitter Bomb and went on to receive considerable attention as a clone. Other numbered El Chivo phenotypes also circulate, however, so the cultivar should not be reduced entirely to #5. The original seed population offers a broader range of blueberry, grape, candy, perfume, kerosene, structure, and color than the celebrated Glitter Bomb clone alone.
Effects and Experience

El Chivo often develops more gradually than its frosted appearance suggests. The beginning can feel cerebral and somewhat buoyant, with mood lifting before the body becomes noticeably heavy. Creative thinking , conversation, music, or visually engaging entertainment may feel more interesting during this early stage because the mental shift tends to arrive before deep sedation. Some selections can feel surprisingly clear and energetic at first, especially when consumed in a moderate amount.

The physical side becomes increasingly important as the session develops. Muscles begin to loosen, movement feels less urgent, and the brighter opening settles into a calmer, more grounded state. With stronger servings, that relaxation can become substantial enough to encourage a long period on the couch or eventually sleep. The transition is usually smoother than an abrupt indica knockout, making the strain more flexible than its later heaviness might imply.

Potency varies considerably across the seed line. Compound Genetics does not assign one universal THC percentage to El Chivo, although elite selections such as #5 have produced cannabinoid results in the upper-20% range. Consumers should therefore judge strength from the actual flower rather than assuming every phenotype behaves identically. Dry mouth and dry eyes are common possibilities, while excessive consumption can bring dizziness, short-term memory disruption, or anxiety before the body-heavy portion of the experience takes over.
Medical Benefits

The strain’s changing effect profile may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer mental uplift followed by stronger physical relaxation. During the earlier stage, the brighter mood can make stress, emotional fatigue, or low motivation feel less intrusive. Later, the heavier body sensation may reduce awareness of muscular tightness or general discomfort, particularly when the cultivar is used in a relaxed setting rather than during demanding daytime activity.

Larger servings may also increase appetite and drowsiness. That can make El Chivo more suitable for evening use among consumers who want marijuana that gradually shifts from mentally engaging to physically quiet. High-potency phenotypes should be treated with caution by people sensitive to THC, because the same cerebral effects that feel euphoric at a low dose can become uncomfortable when consumption rises too quickly.

There is no single standardized terpene profile that applies to every plant grown from El Chivo seed. Selected cuts have shown myrcene, beta-caryophyllene, and linalool among prominent terpenes, but phenotype and cultivation conditions can change the chemistry considerably. Medical cannabis consumers should therefore rely on testing from the specific batch whenever possible and consider cannabinoid strength, medications, tolerance, and personal response rather than assuming every El Chivo harvest will produce the same therapeutic experience.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweet grape is usually the first aromatic reference associated with El Chivo, but the profile is far broader than simple fruit. Blueberry can sit underneath the grape, sometimes resembling dark berry candy or sweet cough syrup, while perfume introduces a light floral quality above the heavier base. The combined fruit notes give well-selected plants a saturated purple-fruit character without losing the pungency expected from Grape Gas ancestry.

Kerosene appears beneath that sweetness and gives the bouquet its sharper identity. Breaking apart a mature flower can release enough fuel to change the entire impression from dessert-like fruit into something closer to grape candy stored beside gasoline. Some phenotypes lean much harder into the gas, while others emphasize blueberry, perfume, or sugary candy. That variation is part of what made the seed line attractive for hunting rather than merely reproducing one predictable aroma.

Flavor tends to follow the same sequence. Grape and blueberry sweetness appear early, followed by darker resin, earth, and fuel on the finish. Vaporization can preserve more of the floral and berry top notes, whereas combustion usually makes the kerosene side more dominant. A controlled dry and patient cure are especially valuable because the delicate perfume and fruit compounds can disappear quickly when flowers lose moisture too aggressively.
Growing Information

Compound Genetics describes El Chivo as having excellent agronomic traits and being comparatively easy to grow. Most phenotypes display long internodal spacing with separated bud sites rather than producing an excessively crowded canopy. That architecture improves light penetration and natural airflow, reducing the amount of heavy defoliation required. Plants move through vegetation at an average pace, giving growers enough time to top or train them before flowering without requiring an unusually long vegetative period.

Indoor flowering generally takes 8–9 weeks. Resin production can become exceptional as maturity approaches, and rich green or purple coloration may develop depending on phenotype and environment. The breeder does not publish a standardized yield figure for the current seed line, so production is better evaluated plant by plant. Strong light, healthy roots, even canopy exposure, and stable irrigation can help growers capitalize on its productive structure without sacrificing terpene quality. Selected cuts such as El Chivo #5 are especially notable for strong stems and an unusually high proportion of premium-looking flower.

Outdoor cultivation benefits from the same open architecture. An 8–9-week bloom generally places maturity between late September and October in many Northern Hemisphere environments, although latitude determines when flowering actually begins. Full sun and generous root space can allow considerable growth, while the natural separation between bud sites helps air move through the plant during cooler autumn conditions. Phenotype hunters may want to evaluate grape intensity, blueberry character, kerosene strength, trichome density, branch strength, color, and flower structure together rather than selecting solely for size.
FAQ
What strains make El Chivo?

El Chivo was bred by Compound Genetics from OGKB Blueberry Headband × Grape Gas. The combination brings together berry-heavy OGKB and Blueberry Headband genetics with the sweet grape, Gelato, and fuel characteristics of Grape Gas.
Is El Chivo the same strain as Glitter Bomb?

Glitter Bomb is El Chivo #5, a specific phenotype selected from the larger El Chivo seed population. Every Glitter Bomb plant traces back to El Chivo #5, but not every El Chivo phenotype is Glitter Bomb.
What does El Chivo taste like?

The breeder describes the line around sweet grapes, blueberry, candy, kerosene gas, and perfume. Individual plants vary, with some emphasizing fruit and floral sweetness while others develop a much stronger fuel character.
How long does El Chivo take to flower?

Compound Genetics lists an indoor flowering period of approximately 8–9 weeks. Outdoor harvest commonly occurs from late September through October depending on local latitude, climate, and the start of natural flowering.
Is El Chivo easy to grow?

Yes. Compound Genetics specifically describes the cultivar as easy to grow and possessing strong agronomic traits. Its separated bud sites and generally open structure help with light penetration and airflow, although maintaining proper humidity remains important once resinous flowers reach full maturity.
Final Thoughts on El Chivo

El Chivo became important because it delivered much more than an attractive grape aroma. OGKB Blueberry Headband gives the cultivar berry depth, Kush influence, and flower quality, while Grape Gas contributes the sweet fruit, kerosene, and modern resin production that define the line. Together they created a population broad enough for phenotype hunting yet consistent enough to establish a recognizable grape-blueberry-gas identity.

Its most famous offspring from that hunt, El Chivo #5, demonstrated how much potential existed inside the cross. Renamed Glitter Bomb, the cut became celebrated for purple flowers, extreme trichome coverage, strong stems, and loud sweet-gas terpenes. That success should not obscure the broader El Chivo family, however, because other phenotypes can express their own combinations of perfume, candy, berry, fuel, structure, and coloration.

For growers, an 8–9-week flowering window, straightforward cultivation, open bud spacing, and exceptional resin potential make this weed strain practical as well as visually impressive. For consumers, the gradual movement from mental uplift toward substantial body relaxation adds depth beyond the aroma. El Chivo ultimately stands as one of Compound Genetics’ more significant grape-and-gas releases—a cannabis line remembered not only for producing Glitter Bomb, but for combining elite bag appeal with reliable garden performance and a flavor profile that remains unmistakably its own.
